question.prompt: A choir director must select a group of singers from among his \(6\) tenors and \(8\) basses. The only requirements are that the difference between the number of tenors and basses must be a multiple of \(4,\) and the group must have at least one singer. Let \(N\) be the number of groups that can be selected. What is the remainder when \(N\) is divided by \(100?\)

solutions.title: Count the unselected basses
solutions.explanation:
Counting the basses who do not sing turns the difference condition into a condition on the size of one subset.

For a choir containing \(t\) tenors and \(b\) basses, form an auxiliary subset consisting of the selected tenors and the unselected basses. Its size is
\[
k=t+(8-b)=8+(t-b).
\]
Thus \(t-b\) is a multiple of \(4\) exactly when \(k\) is a multiple of \(4\).

This correspondence is reversible: from an auxiliary subset, select its tenors and all basses outside it. Consequently, every choir satisfying the difference condition corresponds to exactly one such subset, with no omissions or duplicates.

There are \(14\) singers, so the possible auxiliary subset sizes are \(0,4,8,12\). We must exclude the empty choir. It corresponds to the single auxiliary subset containing all eight basses and no tenors. Therefore
\[
N=\binom{14}{0}+\binom{14}{4}+\binom{14}{8}+\binom{14}{12}-1.
\]
Using \(\binom{14}{8}=\binom{14}{6}\) and \(\binom{14}{12}=\binom{14}{2}\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
N
&=1+\frac{14\cdot13\cdot12\cdot11}{4\cdot3\cdot2\cdot1}
+\frac{14\cdot13\cdot12\cdot11\cdot10\cdot9}{6\cdot5\cdot4\cdot3\cdot2\cdot1}
+\frac{14\cdot13}{2}-1\\
&=1+1001+3003+91-1\\
&=4095.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(4095=40\cdot100+95\), the requested remainder is \(\boxed{95}\), choice \(\text{D}\).
